articles.title: University of California
articles.author: Joe Mathews
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Do you have a brilliant child who makes you proud—but is also a pain in the butt? So does the Golden State. Its great, infuriating child is the University of California. In her terrific new book, California Dreams: The Making and Remaking of the University of California , journalist and author Miriam Pawel (my former L.A. Times colleague) tags all the bases of UC history, from the university’s 1868 founding in the Berkeley Hills through its expansion into a $60 billion educational and economic engine encompassing 10 campuses, six health systems, and three national laboratories. articles.title: Jewish Identity
articles.author: H. Scott Prosterman
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. On December 11, 2019, convicted felon Donald Trump signed Executive Order 13899 , which declared Judaism to be a separate “race” and “ethnicity;” and all Jews of common “national origin.” The purpose was to twist Title VI of the 1964 Civil Rights Act into a tool for speech suppression. It had the “hat trick” effect of patronizing Jews and persecuting Palestinians; and prosecuting an attack on free speech. Indirectly, this was a misappropriation of the Civil Rights Act, and it also undermines the prospects for a two-state solution between Israel and Palestinians. articles.title: Charity Begins at Home
articles.author: Eva Amar
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month, a time to recognize victims, honor survivors, and acknowledge the people and organizations that help them escape abuse. It is also an appropriate time to examine how organizations entrusted with protecting vulnerable people spend their resources. articles.title: Double Standard on War Crimes
articles.author: Marjorie Cohn
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The U.S. government has long sought to incapacitate the International Criminal Court (ICC), the world’s first global court that was created to prosecute the most atrocious crimes. As the ICC seeks to provide accountability for Israeli crimes, the Trump administration has become increasingly aggressive in its attempts to hobble the court. On October 9, 2026, Team Trump imposed punitive sanctions against the court itself, which constitutes the gravest intensification of its war on the ICC. articles.title: Jacobin Is International
articles.author: Asher Dupuy-Spencer
articles.content_excerpt: Jacobin began in the United States, but our emancipatory project has always been internationalist. The questions we’re focused on — about who holds power in our societies, about how capitalism shapes our lives, and how working people can abolish class society — extend across borders. Alongside our English-language magazine, Jacobin publishes regularly in six other languages: Dutch: Jacobin Nederland Greek: Jacobin Greece German: Jacobin Magazin Italian: Jacobin Italia Portuguese: Jacobin Brasil , based in Brazil Spanish: Jacobin América Latina , based in Argentina We’re also working on launching editions in French, Romanian, and Urdu. articles.title: The Video Game Industry’s Crisis Is a Crisis of Capitalism
articles.author: Alexandre Paquet
articles.content_excerpt: Montreal has been touted as a major creative hub for the video game industry for over twenty years, leading the province of Quebec’s efforts to develop its digital creative sector. The industry reportedly generates CAD$1.4 billion in annual revenues within the province, yet game workers feel the lack of job security more than ever. At the end of the summer, games workers rallied in Montreal to support the Bethesda employees affected by recent layoffs. Back in July, Microsoft announced it was eliminating 3,200 jobs within the Xbox division before the end of the year. Among the employees affected is Simon Préfontaine, a designer with over nine years under his belt at Bethesda Montreal. articles.title: Anwar Shaikh Changed My Life
articles.author: E. Ahmet Tonak
articles.content_excerpt: Anwar Shaikh, one of the most important Marxist economists of his generation, died on October 6 at the age of eighty in New York City. Two years ago, a conference was held to mark his retirement from the Department of Economics at the New School for Social Research, where he had taught for fifty years. I was one of the speakers on the first panel. I opened my talk by adapting the famous first line of Orhan Pamuk’s Yeni Hayat ( The New Life ), knowing that Pamuk was one of Anwar’s favorite writers: “I met Anwar Shaikh, and my whole life changed!” That is truly what happened. After the 1971 military coup in Turkey, I went first to Sweden and then came to the United States. articles.title: Tax the Rich and Slash the Military Budget
articles.author: Nancy Folbre
articles.content_excerpt: Here’s a question progressives get asked constantly: Fine, you want universal childcare, Medicare for All, and a green economy — but how are you going to pay for it? As part of the Game Changers project , economists Gerald Epstein and Aaron Medlin just answered it with a full accounting. They price out the thirty policies in the Game Changers initiative and show, line by line, how to fund them without adding a dime to the deficit — by taxing wealth and capital the same way the United States already taxes wages and by shrinking a military and immigration-enforcement budget that is both bloated and destructive. articles.title: The Political Economy of the Restaurant
articles.author: Ed Luker
articles.content_excerpt: English food does not have a good reputation. In 1806, Grimod de La Reynière, a pioneering French food critic, wrote that “[England’s] cooking is limited to boiled chickens.” More than two hundred years later, stereotypes about the country’s food have hardly improved. Looking at the staple icons of English cuisine today — fish and chips, the Sunday roast, the full English breakfast — one might agree with Grimod’s point. These dishes are brutish mounds of meat and carbs, the product of a culture that has often seemed more interested in excess than culinary refinement. They hardly suggest the level of technique and attention to simple, high-quality ingredients associated with French or Japanese food. It’s not only the nation’s cuisine that’s in a sorry state. articles.title: AI Is Coming for You, But You Can Fight Back: The Hidden Costs of Artificial Intelligence
articles.author: Frieda Afary
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Artificial intelligence is being sold to the public as the next great technological revolution, promising unprecedented productivity, scientific breakthroughs, and solutions to some of humanity's most difficult problems. But who benefits from this transformation, who pays its costs, and who gets to decide how the technology is deployed? Those questions drove a panel titled “AI Is Coming for You, But You Can Fight Back” at the fourth annual Left Coast Forum, held October 2–4, 2026, at California State University, Los Angeles. articles.author: Rick Chertoff, Dick Price, Robert Corsini
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The Israeli assault on Gaza cannot be understood by beginning the story on October 7, 2023. That was one of the central arguments advanced during a panel titled “The Gaza Genocide” at the fourth annual Left Coast Forum, held October 2–4, 2026, at California State University, Los Angeles. Featuring longtime Jewish peace activist Rick Chertoff and historian Dr. Mahmood Ibrahim, the discussion challenged familiar narratives about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and examined the history of dispossession, occupation, failed diplomatic initiatives, and American military support that preceded the current catastrophe. articles.title: Workers Can Govern, but They Need Power First
articles.author: Jared Abbott
articles.content_excerpt: According to data from a sweeping new study of working-class legislators by political scientists Nicholas Carnes and Noam Lupu, only about 2 percent of legislators across the world’s democracies held a working-class job — which the authors define as manual, service, or clerical work — before getting into politics. Yet as the authors document in their new book , Keeping Workers Off the Ballot: How Democracy Undermines Working-Class Representation , about seven in ten jobs in a typical democracy are working-class jobs, from construction workers and truck drivers to servers, cashiers, receptionists, data-entry clerks, day laborers, and street vendors. articles.title: What Happens to Art
articles.author: William J. Astore
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. There’s a kerfuffle about art being political, with journalists and writers I respect, such as Matt Taibbi and Caitlin Johnstone , coming down on opposite sides of the issue. Johnstone puts it bluntly : “I have no respect for this idea that art is somehow separable from politics. articles.title: Colombia’s President Wants US Boots on the Ground
articles.author: Carlos Cruz Mosquera
articles.content_excerpt: In the ten weeks since multimillionaire lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella was inaugurated as Colombia’s president, the country has undergone a significant political shift with respect to asserting its national sovereignty, with Colombia returning to — and potentially deepening — its subordinate position vis-à-vis the United States. Less than a week after the change of government in Colombia, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced a major shift in US-Colombian military cooperation, stating at a press conference that de la Espriella had approved an agreement for joint operations in Colombia. articles.title: Italian Students Join French
articles.author: Phil Pasquini
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Italian high school and university students along with teachers demonstrated and marched during a consolidated nationwide day-long school strike across the country on October 16. The students have been inspired by the recent French student blockades and protests and in reaction to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s proposed cuts in educational spending along with a recently adopted decree-law which has banned the wearing of face coverings including burqas and niqabs in class.
